diagram:
flowchart TD
  TRIG["▶ On-demand / batch
single symbol or top 3 watchlist"] --> RUN["🤖 Standalone AV + LLM pass
NOT the research pipeline"]
  RUN --> LABEL["🏷️ Write agent_signals
agent_label='deepseek' · score_source='llm_advisory'"]
  LABEL --> QUAR["🚧 Quarantined from execution
PaperTrader allowlists deterministic_v1 only"]
  QUAR --> READBACK["👁️ GET last 10 rows
the only surface that reads these"]
  RUN -.->|"premise void"| PREMISE["⚠️ Nothing to A/B against
primary research is ALSO DeepSeek"]

TRIG.label: On-demand / batch
TRIG.description: Runs a single symbol (body.symbol) or, with no symbol, batches the top 3 research-enabled watchlist names ordered by created_at. Not a scheduled cron — no vercel.json or pg_cron entry exists. Accepts a cron-secret bypass, otherwise gated to the owner account.
TRIG.addReason: A/B is exploratory — run to sample comparison data.
TRIG.changeReason: Batch mode fixed: was ordering by a non-existent added_at column (0 rows → 400); now filters research_enabled + orders by created_at.

RUN.label: Standalone AV + LLM pass
RUN.description: Does NOT share any code with the research pipeline. It fetches Alpha Vantage COMPANY_OVERVIEW + RSI and hands them to a single prompt that asks the MODEL to produce action / confidence / analyst_score itself — the exact design the main system deliberately abandoned, where all 5 scores are computed deterministically and the LLM writes only the thesis. No dimensions, no availability mask, no weights, no champion, no direction gate, no research_packets. Its model is hardcoded 'deepseek-v4-flash', an id that never existed at the API and which the router's legacy alias rewrites to deepseek-chat — so it is the one agent whose model is NOT per-flow configurable from Settings.
RUN.addReason: Cheap A/B: is DeepSeek good enough to scale on?
RUN.changeReason: Claimed to run 'the same research/scoring pipeline but with the DeepSeek LLM'. It shares nothing with that pipeline and inverts its core principle by letting the model generate the numbers.

LABEL.label: agent_label = deepseek
LABEL.description: Inserts into agent_signals with agent_label='deepseek', agent_type='deepseek-research', status='advisory', and score_source='llm_advisory'. Writes no per-dimension scores, no market, and no research_packet_id — so a like-for-like comparison against primary signals is not actually possible from these rows. It can also emit direction='hold', a value nothing else in the system produces.
LABEL.addReason: Labeled rows enable the comparison UI.
LABEL.changeReason: The rows exist but are not comparable: the fields a side-by-side would need are never written. Documented score_source, which is what actually keeps these rows away from money.

QUAR.label: Quarantined from execution
QUAR.description: These signals structurally cannot become trades: PaperTrader selects on score_source='deterministic_v1' as a POSITIVE allowlist, so an advisory LLM row is excluded by construction rather than by a negative filter that would fail open if a new source appeared.
QUAR.addReason: The one genuinely load-bearing property of this agent — that its LLM-generated scores cannot reach a fill — was nowhere on the diagram.

READBACK.label: GET last 10 rows
READBACK.description: The only surface that reads these signals: GET /api/agents/deepseek-research returns the last 10 agent_label='deepseek' rows. There is no comparison UI and no outcome attribution.
READBACK.addReason: Replaces the COMPARE node's claim of a comparison card with the read path that actually exists.

PREMISE.label: Premise void
PREMISE.description: This agent was built to answer 'is the cheap model good enough to replace the expensive primary?'. That question is dead: primary research already runs DeepSeek (deepseek-reasoner, per-flow from Settings). This agent runs the cheaper sibling (deepseek-chat, via a legacy alias) on a different, LLM-generates-the-numbers pipeline — so any comparison would be DeepSeek-tier vs DeepSeek-tier across two incomparable designs. Kept on the diagram as an explicit warning rather than deleted, because the code still runs and still writes rows.
PREMISE.addReason: A vestigial agent that silently writes signals is more dangerous undocumented than documented. Flagging the dead premise is the honest state; the deprecate-or-delete call is the owner's, not the diagram's.

history.label: 'Same research pipeline via DeepSeek' is false — it is a standalone AV+LLM scorer
history.reason: The node claimed this runs 'the same research/scoring pipeline but with the DeepSeek LLM, to measure signal quality vs the primary model'. It shares ZERO code with lib/research-agent.ts. It fetches Alpha Vantage COMPANY_OVERVIEW + RSI and asks the model to emit action/confidence/analyst_score itself — the inverse of the main pipeline's contract, where all 5 dimensions are computed deterministically and the LLM writes thesis narrative only. No dimensions, availability mask, weights, champion, direction gate, or research_packets. This mattered beyond wording: a reader comparing 'deepseek' rows against primary rows would think they were reading one pipeline under two models, when they are reading two different epistemologies. Also recorded that its model is hardcoded 'deepseek-v4-flash' — an id that never existed at the DeepSeek API — which the router's legacy alias silently rewrites to deepseek-chat, making it the only agent whose model is NOT per-flow configurable from Settings.

history.label: 'AgentComparisonCard shows DeepSeek vs primary' — that card does not do this
history.reason: Removed, not edited: the node described a UI that does not exist. AgentComparisonCard is a US-vs-India paper-performance card (header 'Market Comparison · Paper Performance · US vs India', typed MarketStat{market}) — it has no DeepSeek concept at all. There is no DeepSeek-vs-primary comparison surface and no outcome attribution anywhere in the app; the only read path is GET /api/agents/deepseek-research returning the last 10 labelled rows, now drawn as READBACK. The mermaid edge also named 'primary (Claude/Groq)', neither of which is on the research scoring path. Note execClaude is NOT deleted repo-wide — it survives in the trader, ai, live-account/refresh-snapshot, and mentor routes; it was removed only from the research screener, where it structurally could not work and had been silently returning [] on every run.

history.label: 'Which LLM scores better' — the question is void; replaced by PREMISE
history.reason: The node's 'advisory / does not change the live model automatically' half was TRUE and is now enforced structurally rather than by convention, so that property was preserved on the new QUAR node rather than dropped. But 'determines whether DeepSeek's cheaper scoring matches the primary before scaling it up' is false in every part: nothing determines it (no comparison, no attribution), and the premise collapsed when primary research became DeepSeek — this agent runs the cheaper sibling on an incomparable pipeline, so the 'A/B' is DeepSeek-tier vs DeepSeek-tier across two different designs. Replaced with an explicit PREMISE warning node rather than silently deleted, because the route still runs and still writes agent_signals rows; a vestigial writer is more dangerous undocumented than documented. Whether to deprecate or delete the agent is the owner's call, not the diagram's.

history.label: Advisory rows are structurally fenced out of execution
history.reason: The single most load-bearing fact about this agent was absent from its diagram: its LLM-generated scores cannot become trades. PaperTrader selects .eq('score_source','deterministic_v1') — a POSITIVE allowlist, chosen over a negative filter precisely because a negative filter fails OPEN the moment a new score_source appears. Drawn explicitly so that anyone reading 'this agent writes agent_signals' can see immediately why that is safe, rather than having to trust it. Paired with READBACK, which documents the only surface that consumes these rows.

history.label: Rows exist but are not comparable — the comparison fields are never written
history.reason: 'Writes signals tagged agent_label=deepseek so they can be compared side-by-side' is half true. The tag and the insert are real; the comparability is not. The row carries no per-dimension scores, no market, and no research_packet_id — the exact fields a side-by-side against a primary signal would need. It can also emit direction='hold', a value no other producer emits and no consumer handles. Added score_source='llm_advisory' to the description because that field, not the label, is what actually governs whether the row can touch money.

history.label: Verified accurate — trigger behaviour unchanged since the 07-04 fix
history.reason: Re-verified against code rather than assumed: single symbol via body.symbol, else batch of top 3 watchlist names filtered on research_enabled and ordered by created_at. The 2026-07-04 added_at→created_at fix is real and still in place. Confirmed 'not a scheduled cron' is still TRUE — no entry in vercel.json and none in pg_cron. Description amended only to record the cron-secret bypass and the owner gate; no behavioural claim changed.
